context.context: SKETCH: Suppose the cone were smaller. A cone with one gate fewer than its variables allow reads each of its variables once. Take the lowest gate joining the two ends of a lost edge: it is an AND with only ORs above it inside the cone, and it is not below the function, so it holds a further variable; do the same for a second lost edge; the two ANDs and the single-vertex part need more reads than a read-once cone has, or the partner condition puts a non-edge below the function. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

context.title: 4-cycle-free bipartite stop-form AND/OR circuits: a private-cone gate whose lost edges its top-AND partner sees has cone >= |lin c| + |V(Lost c)|
context.unlocks: A lower bound on the cone of a reused gate in a normal-form circuit: with it, exchanging such a gate for stars never gains a gate, a step toward 'a least circuit that cannot be improved is two-level'.

public_research.plain_statement: Bipartite incidence, no 4-cycle; C: AND/OR gates each reading exactly two earlier wires, computing the edge function, in stop form. c: a gate not below the function whose cone no outside gate reads. lin(c): inputs v with c true at v alone. Lost(c): edges C accepts that are lost when c becomes constant false, ends outside lin(c). If both are nonempty and each lost edge has an end at which the other input of some top AND (below the function) reading c is true alone, then the cone of c (with c) has at least |lin c| + |ends of Lost c| gates.
